newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldiers disappear at dawn's first crack.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldiers disappear at dawn's first crack.

text.p: "Get out. By God, you should never come back," a young Palestinian shouted on Friday as Israeli soldiers pulled out of Hebron's military headquarters by dawn's early light.
It took fewer than five minutes for the last contingent of Israeli soldiers to leave the compound, a much-hated symbol of 30 years of occupation.
The Israelis jumped into their jeeps and disappeared.
And the PLO police moved in to take over 80 percent of the West Bank town.
The young Palestinian man had endured a rainy and cold night outside the military compound. He wanted to capture the crucial moment.

Israeli soldiers and PLO policemen in plain clothes together struggled during the hours before the Israeli departure to keep a small crowd of Palestinians and journalists from blocking the narrow road out of the military headquarters.
More than rejoicing, a sombre mood gripped the nearly 100 Palestinians who surged into the long-forbidden grounds of the compound curiously surveying it after the pullout.
Toddlers scurried around the building looking for bullet shells that Israeli soldiers may have left behind.
Palestinians who had been jailed by Israel sought to revisit the cells where they had been held.

A young Palestinian, tucking the red, white, green and black Palestinian national colours in his back pocket, climbed a 15 metre (50 foot)-high antenna left by the Israelis above the building and planted the flag on top.
Except for a few salvos of fireworks set off by enthusiastic supporters of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, there were few signs of joy.
"This is an historic day. This is the day we have waited for all these years," said Abdel-Hamid Farajallah, a disabled Palestinian touring the site.
"There is nothing as bad as being under occupation," the 48-year-old man said as the sun rose in the sky.
"We thank God that we have a state and an army who are our brethren to protect us," said 65-year-old Hussein Awaiwi, who lives near the Hebron market.
There, on New Year's Day, an off-duty Israeli soldier shot and wounded seven Palestinians in a bid to stop the handover.
"But our joy will not be complete until we see the settlers leave the heart of our city," he said.
